research_rationale: EO 11046 (27 FR 8575, signed 1962-08-24; held official Federal Register text, page location high) authorizes the Secretaries of the military departments (and the Coast Guard's Secretary) to award the Bronze Star Medal (paragraph 1 with subparagraphs (a)-(c)), sets design and regulations (2), limits to one medal with devices (3), allows posthumous award (4), and supersedes EO 9419 while keeping existing regulations until replaced (5). It rests on the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief, not on a statute, so no authority statute can have lapsed. The held original has no sunset, expiry, condition subsequent or revocation. Later instruments found by name or by number in the held texts: EO 11382 section 13 (1967-11-28; Treasury to Transportation in paragraph 1), EO 13286 section 70 (68 FR 10619; effective 2003-03-01; Transportation to Homeland Security in section 1) and EO 14085 section 4 (87 FR 60541, signed 2022-10-03; paragraph 1 wording, Space Force). All three amend paragraph 1 only and none revokes or supersedes the order. The held current-law extract of the Code (release point 119-121; only the extracted note text is held, so it is corroboration and not a claim source) prints the order in full as a note to 10 U.S.C. 7276, as amended by those three orders, with no ending statement. The ofr_catalog search reports three hits for this order, which are exactly these three amendments. Cutoff limit: the held Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected.
savings_reason: The order has not ended, so no residual outlasting an end arises. Its only savings text is the second sentence of paragraph 5 (existing regulations under EO 9419 remain in effect until modified or revoked by regulations prescribed under this order), decided separately as clause EO:11046#c-5. None of the three bounded searches names an instrument that revokes, replaces or ends that sentence.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end is held. The order has no own-terms end: the word until appears only in paragraph 5, where it limits how long the pre-1962 regulations are preserved, not how long the order's commands run. A search of the held texts for the number 11046 finds EO 11382, EO 13286, EO 14085 and the held current-law note extract (all amendments or printings), plus the 1989 OFR codification line treating the order as in force. The packet's chain also labels one amendment as EO 12977, but the held text under that label (a source-ladder file named for EO 12977) is EO 13286 section 70; the official text of EO 12977 (Interagency Security Committee) does not mention EO 11046, so EO 12977 is not recorded as an event.
scope_check: EO 11382 and EO 13286 change only the officer named in paragraph 1 (and in 11382 the same words wherever they appear in the listed orders). EO 14085 section 4 amends paragraph 1 only: its item (a) (Transportation to Homeland Security) could not be executed because EO 13286 had already made that change (note in the held extract), and items (b)-(d) change who is eligible and add the Space Force. Paragraphs 2-5 have no held amendment; the held current-law note extract prints them unchanged. Under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 each amendment is a later event on the clause it changes and the clause continues.
independent_command_check: Paragraph 1 (award authority and eligible persons), 2 (design and regulations), 3 (one medal, devices), 4 (posthumous award) and 5 (supersession of EO 9419 and preservation of existing regulations) are separate commands. Subparagraphs (a)-(c) are the three eligibility situations of paragraph 1. Each is decided on its own; none is exhausted by performance because each governs awards that continue to be made.
savings_check: See savings reason. The supersession sentence of paragraph 5 took effect with the order and is retained in the held current-law note extract; the preservation sentence is a standing rule that no held instrument repeals or amends, so it is recorded as operative without any claim about which old regulations still survive.

research_rationale: EO 11079 (28 FR 819, signed 1963-01-25; held official Federal Register text, page location high) is a single designation made under section 2603 of title 10, United States Code: the Secretary of Defense (Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps members), the Secretary of the Treasury (Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy) and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare (commissioned officers of the Public Health Service) are to prescribe regulations under which members may accept fellowships, scholarships or grants, uniform so far as practicable. The held original has no sunset, expiry, condition or revocation. Three later orders changed the officers named: EO 11382 section 13 (1967-11-28; Treasury to Transportation), EO 12608 section 15 (1987-09-09; Health, Education, and Welfare to Health and Human Services) and EO 13286 section 69 (effective 2003-03-01; Transportation to Homeland Security). None revokes or supersedes the order. The held current-law extract of the Code (only the extracted note text is held, so it is corroboration and not a claim source) prints the order as amended by all three as a note to 10 U.S.C. 2603, so the authority section named in the order is still in the Code, and the note carries no ending statement. The ofr_catalog search reports three hits for this order, which are the three amendments. Cutoff limit: the held Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected.
savings_reason: The held original contains no savings, transitional or residual-effects clause, and none of the three later amendments adds one.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end is held. The order has no own-terms end. A search of the held texts for the number 11079 finds EO 11382, EO 12608, EO 13286, the held current-law note extract and the 1989 OFR codification line treating the order as in force. The packet's chain also labels one amendment as EO 12977, but the held text under that label (a source-ladder file named for EO 12977) is EO 13286 section 69; the official text of EO 12977 does not mention EO 11079, so EO 12977 is not recorded as an event.
scope_check: Each amendment substitutes an officer's title in the single designation; none changes what the designees are to do. The held current-law note extract prints the designation with the three substitutions and otherwise unchanged. Under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 each is a later event and the clause continues.
independent_command_check: The order is one command (designation to prescribe regulations) naming three designees for three groups of persons; the three designations cannot end separately on the held evidence, and each continues with its current officer.
savings_check: See savings reason; no savings text exists, and regulations issued by the designees rest on the designation and do not make it exhausted.

research_rationale: EO 11231 (30 FR 8665, signed 1965-07-08; held official Federal Register text, page location high) establishes the Vietnam Service Medal (section 1), lets members who qualified for the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal by Vietnam service between July 1, 1958 and July 4, 1965 remain qualified for it or exchange it on application for the Vietnam Service Medal (section 2) and allows posthumous award (section 3). It rests on the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief, not on a statute. No Code note prints this order, so no CURRENT record is held; the current predicate therefore rests on the route original plus bounded searches: the held original, every held later instrument attached as an event, no own-terms end, and the three bounded machine searches read for their stated coverage. Later instruments: EO 11382 section 13 (1967-11-28; Treasury to Transportation in section 1) and EO 13286 section 66 (effective 2003-03-01; Transportation to Homeland Security in section 1). Neither revokes or supersedes the order, and the ofr_catalog disposition record held in jobs/peano-formulario lists exactly these two amendments and no revocation. Own-terms signal: section 1 awards the medal for service 'before a terminal date to be prescribed by the Secretary of Defense'. That is a limit on which service qualifies, set under the order itself; the same held OFR record notes that the terminal date was set as March 28, 1973 by the Secretary of Defense (DoD Instruction 1348.15 memo of January 26, 1973) and that service after it did not qualify. It does not end the command to award the medal for qualifying service or the exchange right in section 2: the held current Army regulation AR 600-8-22 (a source-ladder capture of the edition that supersedes the 30 July 2025 edition) says in its paragraph 2-13 that the Vietnam Service Medal 'was established by EO 11231, 8 July 1965, as amended by EO 13286', is awarded for service in Vietnam after 3 July 1965 through 28 March 1973, and that on request a person qualified for the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal may be awarded the Vietnam Service Medal instead. That regulation is held in the repository but is not one of the packet's citable evidence records, so it is described here and not used as a claim source. Cutoff limit: the bounded Code and eCFR searches were run for the cutoff but this order has no hit in the Code notes; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected in the held Code edition (current through 2026-10-09).
savings_reason: The order has not ended, so no residual outlasting an end arises. Its only savings-type text is section 2 (members qualified for the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal by Vietnam service remain qualified), decided as its own clause; no later instrument held ends or changes it.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end is held. The only own-terms time limit is the terminal date in section 1, discussed in the rationale: it limits qualifying service and was set by the Secretary of Defense; it is not an end date for the order or for the command to award the medal for qualifying service. A search of the held texts for the number 11231 finds EO 11382, EO 13286, the 1989 OFR codification line and the OFR disposition record. The packet's chain also labels one amendment as EO 12977, but the held text under that label is EO 13286 section 66; the official text of EO 12977 does not mention EO 11231, so EO 12977 is not recorded as an event. The four own-term records attached to the dossier (fixed_term and until_event) are fragments of an unrelated Army Board for Correction of Military Records decision about one applicant, not wording of this order.
scope_check: EO 11382 and EO 13286 change only the officer named in section 1 (the Secretary who prescribes Coast Guard regulations). Sections 2 and 3 have no held amendment. Each amendment is a later event on section 1 and the clause continues (strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21).
independent_command_check: The preamble (authority recital), section 1 (establishment and award rule), section 2 (qualification and exchange rules) and section 3 (posthumous award) are separate. Each is decided on its own; none is exhausted by performance because awards under each continue to be made.
savings_check: See savings reason. Section 2 preserves earlier Expeditionary Medal qualification and is itself operative.
